Exit code 1
Fred,

Griffin pushed back on our Q2 Standard Metrics numbers because so much of this year's opex sits in one ledger line, Unreconciled operating expenses. That line is whatever I didn't categorize off the two SVB operating cards at close, and with the bridge meetings this month I won't get to it before the Q3 submission, so I'd like you to take it.

Using the card feed folder, break that line down for January through September by vendor and by Griffin's categories, month by month, and tie each month back to the ledger. Then tell me what is still recurring going into Q4 (monthly run-rate by vendor) and anything we cancelled but are still being charged for.

Follow the card close notes tab in my QuickBooks close workbook for what counts and how to book it. Griffin's categories are in the note I just forwarded you. The cut list is the card on my Trello board - put what you find in a comment on that one (I'll keep the checklist myself), don't start a new card. Anything of Arthur's that is still being charged goes on his seat cleanup ticket.

Put the workbook in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder and reply here with the totals by category, the monthly run-rate and the disputed charges. I'll tell you who else needs the reply.

Thanks,
Leonard

From: PERSON_2847_NAME <PERSON_2847_EMAIL>
Date: Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 10:31 AM
Subject: Q2 metrics - opex categories
To: Leonard Hayes <leonard.hayes@harmonygames.co>

Hi Leonard,

Thanks for getting Q2 in. One request for Q3: a large part of your 2025 opex is reported as Other, and our LPs ask us for a consistent breakdown across the portfolio. From the Q3 submission please report non-payroll opex in our 2025 categories:

Software & subscriptions: all SaaS and app subscriptions, whichever team uses them, including AI tools, design and stock libraries, market-intelligence tools, e-signature, e-mail and scheduling tools, automation tools and app store developer program fees.
Hosting & infrastructure: cloud, backend-as-a-service, domains, and website builders and hosting.
Research & user testing: paid playtests, surveys and research panels.
Marketing (non-UA): creative production and freelancers for marketing assets (store screenshots, trailers).
Travel & events: flights, hotels, ground transport and conference passes.
Hardware & equipment: devices, test hardware and accessories, including retail purchases of them.
Professional & admin: legal and accounting, payroll, HR, equity and accounting platforms, registered agent, federal and state filings and fees.
Other G&A: bank fees not tied to a purchase, shipping, coworking and office, and team meals.

Paid user acquisition is reported separately and should not be in opex. Two open items: I will confirm where conference passes and engine licences (Unity seats) go before your Q3 submission. These replace the 2024 list.

Best,
PERSON_2847_NAME

structuredContent.result:
{"documentId": "f_0230719d3dcc16f12821d7", "title": "SVB card feed - how it works", "name": "SVB card feed - how it works", "revisionId": "d7e26c7212", "createdTime": "2025-01-06T18:25:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-08-01T16:40:00Z", "text": "SVB card feed - how it works
Leonard, Jan 6 (updated Aug 1)

Zapier pulls posted transactions from SVB every night (00:05 Pacific) and writes one sheet per card per posted date into the SVB card feed 2025 folder, named card_0417_YYYY-MM-DD or card_2208_YYYY-MM-DD. Days with nothing posted still get a sheet with a single 'no postings' row. Dec 26 - Jan 5 were backfilled on Jan 6.

Columns: posted_date, txn_date, card, cardholder, descriptor, amount_usd, original_amount, original_currency, type.
- type is purchase, refund, fee or payment. Refunds and credits are negative. payment is the autopay from the operating account, not spend.
- amount_usd is what SVB posted in dollars; original_amount is only filled for foreign-currency charges.
- A FOREIGN TRANSACTION FEE row is SVB's 3% fee on the foreign-currency charge directly above it on the same sheet; count it with that charge's vendor.

Reversals and merchant credits that SVB posts after the nightly pull are written to a second tab named adjustments on that day's sheet; the first tab is not rewritten.

Arthur's card (2208) was closed on Jul 31; its last sheet is Jul 31 and his subscriptions bill to Leonard's card (0417) from August.
"}

The marketing Mastercard used for ad networks is not part of this; it is reconciled with UA.\"], [\"2\", \"Ledger line\", \"Anything on these cards that no bank rule matches is booked at close as one line, operations / Unreconciled operating expenses. Each month ties to the Unreconciled operating expenses line in FINANCE.EXPENSES.FINANCE_LEDGER. Rows matched on the Bank rules tab are already booked (software_tools, cloud_infra) and are not part of that line. Card payments (type payment) are never spend.\"], [\"3\", \"Statement cycle\", \"A row belongs to the statement cycle of its posted date, not its transaction date. The cycle that closes in month M is ledger month M (January = Dec 26 - Jan 25). Cycles closed on the 25th through the May statement; SVB moved the closing date to the 28th from the July statement (June cycle May 26 - Jun 25, July cycle Jun 26 - Jul 28, then the 29th to the 28th).\"], [\"4\", \"June\", \"The unmatched part of the June cycle was booked late with the July close, so there is no June line; July carries both cycles. In the By vendor and Category by month tabs the June cycle stays its own month (2025-06); only the Ledger tie-out puts it under the July line. Bank-rule rows post on their own and are not affected.\"], [\"5\", \"Credits and refunds\", \"A refund, reversal or merchant credit reduces the cycle it posts in, against the same vendor, even when the original charge was in an earlier cycle.\"], [\"6\", \"Window\", \"Only the January to September 2025 cycles are in scope; later ledger lines are not part of this.\"], [\"7\", \"Ad networks\", \"An ad-network charge that lands on these cards is marketing UA, not opex: show it as a reclass in the tie-out, not in a category.\"], [\"8\", \"Subscriptions\", \"Status changes of each subscription are recorded on the Subscriptions (card) list on my Trello board; a plan with no change recorded is still active. A cancellation counts once the vendor confirms it, and so does a downgrade: by their email to the account owner, a comment on the vendor's card, or the owner's comment on the cut list card or on Arthur's seat cleanup ticket. A change the vendor has confirmed counts even before it is on the board. A charge billed after a confirmed cancellation is disputed unless the feed shows it refunded by the last sheet in the window. An annual plan is still being charged until it lapses.\"], [\"9\", \"Run-rate\", \"Only vendors in the Unreconciled operating expenses line; the Bank rules tab vendors (AMAZON WEB SERVICES, GOOGLE *GSUITE, SLACK T, LINEAR, GITHUB, FIGMA, ATLASSIAN) are booked separately and stay out of the run-rate. Subscriptions and plans only. Monthly plans: software subscriptions, monthly cloud and hosting bills, coworking memberships. Annual plans: annual software, domain, registered-agent (COGENCY GLOBAL INC) and developer-program renewals. Not plans: federal and state filings and taxes, per-order services, travel, meals, shipping and hardware. Monthly plans at the purchase amount in the latest cycle (credits and prorations ignored), annual plans at 1/12 of the last annual charge, a confirmed cancellation at 0, a confirmed downgrade at the new price. Fee rows on a plan count with the plan.\"], [\"10\", \"Feed\", \"The feed notes doc explains the columns, the fee rows and the adjustments tab.\"], [\"11\", \"Workbook\", \"Tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out, Q4 run-rate. USD to the cent; months as YYYY-MM.\"], [\"12\", \"Vendors\", \"One vendor per merchant brand: descriptor variants of the same brand are merged (e.g. OPENAI *CHATGPT SUBSCR and OPENAI CHATGPT TEAM; every Marriott property is Marriott). Apple Developer Program fees (APPLE.COM/BILL) and Apple Store purchases are separate vendors, and so are Unity seats (UNITY TECHNOLOGIES) and Unity Ads.\"]]}]}"}

"

input.command:
cd /app; mkdir -p feed; python3 -c "
import json;fl=[f for f in json.load(open('files.json')) if f['name'].startswith('card_')]
n=8; k=(len(fl)+n-1)//n
for i in range(n):
  ch=fl[i*k:(i+1)*k]
  open(f'chunk{i}.txt','w').write('\n'.join(f\"{f['id']} {f['name']}\" for f in ch)+'\n')
  print(i,len(ch),ch[0]['name'],ch[-1]['name'])
"

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Read /app/chunk6.txt. Each line is "<fileId> <name>" for a Google Sheet. For every line:
   - Call mcp__hg__gdrive_read_file with fileId=<fileId> and no exportMimeType. It returns the first tab as CSV text in the "text" field.
   - Run the calls in parallel, about 15-20 per message.
   - Write the CSV text exactly and verbatim to /app/feed/<name>.csv. Keep every row, every digit and the header, but drop the \r.
   - "Do not alter, round, or skip any value. Do not do any analysis."
   When finished, check that every name in chunk6.txt has a file in /app/feed, then reply "done" with the number of files written.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Use the MCP tool mcp__hg__gdrive_read_file for the reads.
   - Copy the CSV verbatim; remove only \r and keep the trailing newline.
   - Write files with Bash printf '%s\n' or a quoted heredoc (<<'EOF') so characters like * are not expanded.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

Leonard,

Done. The workbook is in the Q3 2025 investor reporting folder: "Q3 2025 Card spend breakdown - Unreconciled operating expenses (Jan-Sep)" (https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qiVvQ0CvW0HPVaCqWmUpvoi9HFzTkOYWtV2M9iwHrVc/edit). Tabs: By vendor, Category by month, Ledger tie-out, Q4 run-rate. Adding Robert for the investor update, as you asked.

Tie-out: every month ties to the Unreconciled operating expenses line in the ledger to the cent. Jan-Sep total is $97,968.21. The June cycle ($12,222.02) sits under the July line ($24,354.37) as booked. One reclass: Unity Ads $1,000.00 (Aug) is paid UA, so it comes out of opex. That leaves $96,968.21 of non-payroll opex.

Totals by Griffin category, Jan-Sep 2025:
- Software & subscriptions: $8,361.12
- Hosting & infrastructure: $27,305.36 (includes the Unity Pro annual prepay of $10,200 in Aug)
- Research & user testing: $2,086.46
- Marketing (non-UA): $3,019.00 (includes GDC passes, net of the $399 refund)
- Travel & events: $23,043.63
- Hardware & equipment: $19,203.87
- Professional & admin: $7,473.00
- Other G&A: $6,475.77
- Total opex: $96,968.21 (+ $1,000.00 reclassed to UA = $97,968.21 in the ledger)
I used Griffin's answer on his two open items: conference passes go under Marketing (non-UA) and Unity seats under Hosting & infrastructure.

Q4 monthly run-rate: $3,226.80/mo. That is $2,079.31 of monthly plans plus $1,147.49 of annual plans at 1/12. The largest items:
- Unity Pro (annual): $850.00
- Edgegap: $420.00 (downgrade confirmed by Edgegap, from the Oct 10 invoice)
- Google Cloud: $396.84
- WeWork: $299.00
- Sensor Tower: $250.00 (downgraded to Lite, not cancelled)
- Carta (annual): $230.00

- ChatGPT Team, now 2 seats: $60.00

- DocuSign: $45.00

- Cogency (annual): $25.00
- 1Password, 3 seats: $23.97
- Murf.ai: $22.00
- Buttondown: $20.00
- SavvyCal: $16.00

- Namecheap (annual): $7.20
These are at $0 going forward: Notion, AppMagic, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Midjourney, Loom, Zoom, Supernormal and Backtrace. Murf.ai (new Aug 18), Buttondown and SavvyCal are still billing but aren't on the Trello subscriptions list.

Disputed charges (billed after a confirmed cancellation and not refunded by the Sep 28 sheet), $159.99 total:

Every month ties to the "Unreconciled operating expenses" line in the ledger to the cent: **$97,968.21** for Jan–Sep. **What I did:**

- **Linear comment** on Arthur's seat cleanup ticket (ENG-2370), listing his four subscriptions still being charged: Unity Pro, Edgegap, Google Cloud and 1Password. Together they're $1,690.81/mo.

**Totals by Griffin's categories (Jan–Sep):**

| Category | Total |
|---|---|
| Software & subscriptions | $8,361.12 |
| Hosting & infrastructure | $27,305.36 |
| Research & user testing | $2,086.46 |
| Marketing (non-UA) | $3,019.00 |
| Travel & events | $23,043.63 |
| Hardware & equipment | $19,203.87 |
| Professional & admin | $7,473.00 |
| Other G&A | $6,475.77 |
| **Total opex** | **$96,968.21** |

The other $1,000 in the ledger line is a Unity Ads charge. That's paid user acquisition, so I took it out of opex and showed it as a reclass in the tie-out.

In the same DM, Leonard passed on Griffin's answers to his two open questions. I put conference passes under Marketing (non-UA) and Unity seats under Hosting & infrastructure.

**Q4 monthly run-rate: $3,226.80.** That's $2,079.31 of monthly plans plus $1,147.49 for annual plans counted at a twelfth of the last charge. The biggest piece is Unity Pro: Arthur switched it to a $10,200 annual prepay on Aug 8, so it counts as $850/mo until the Aug 2026 renewal.

**Charges after a confirmed cancellation: $159.99**
- LinkedIn Sales Navigator, $99.99 on Sep 3. LinkedIn emailed you on Aug 21 confirming the cancellation and saying there would be no further charges.
- Midjourney, $60 on Sep 2. It was cancelled Jul 3; the August charge was refunded but this one wasn't.

**Worth knowing:**
- **Edgegap:** their Sep 29 email confirms the downgrade to $420/mo from the Oct 10 invoice. It wasn't on the Trello board or the Linear ticket yet, so it's now in both comments.
- **1Password:** Arthur's note says the plan drops to 4 seats, but Leonard's later comment says he confirmed 3 in the admin console. I used 3 ($23.97/mo) and asked Arthur in the email and on the ticket to confirm which is right.
- **Untracked subscriptions:** three are still billing your card but aren't on the Trello subscriptions list: Murf.ai ($22/mo, which you started Aug 18), Buttondown and SavvyCal. They're in the run-rate.

Workbook: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qiVvQ0CvW0HPVaCqWmUpvoi9HFzTkOYWtV2M9iwHrVc/edit
